### Observed differences

- In the later window, activity A10 appears in about 7.5% of traces, down from about 35%; its mean occurrences per trace fell from 0.355 to 0.075. [OCC001, POS001, REL001]
- A25's outgoing behaviour changed sharply: before, it led to A35, A36, A41 and A42 in roughly equal shares (about 25% each); after, about 99% of its outgoing transitions go to A27. [DIR002]
- A26's outgoing behaviour also changed: before, about 99% went to A30; after, A30 is absent and A26 leads to A35, A36, A41 and A42 (about 18–30% each). [DIR003]
- A35, A36, A41 and A42 previously each had about 24% of outgoing transitions to A27; in the later window A27 is no longer a successor, and A30 appears as a successor for each of them (about 21–27%). [DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]
- Order relations reversed for A26 and A27 relative to A35/A36/A41/A42: before, those activities almost always preceded A26 and A27; after, A26 and A27 almost always precede them. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017]
- The lag between A25 and A27 changed from about 5 steps in nearly all cases to 1 step in about 99% of cases. [LAG006]
- The lag between A26 and A30 changed from 1 step in about 99% of cases to 5 steps in about 99% of cases. [LAG007]
- A45's routing changed: before, about 30% of its outgoing transitions went to A10 and about 30–39% to A19/A20; after, only about 2% go to A10 and about 47–46% go to A19/A20. [DIR008, REL009, LAG010]
- Positional shifts are consistent: A26 and A27 moved earlier in traces (mean position from about 0.62 to 0.52 and 0.48 to 0.37), while A35, A36, A41 and A42 moved later (mean position from about 0.41 to 0.58). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural reordering in which A10 is largely absent from most later cases, A25 now routes to A27 instead of to A35/A36/A41/A42, A26 and A27 occur before A35/A36/A41/A42 rather than after them, and A30 occurs later, after those activities, instead of immediately after A26. The direct routing, order and lag evidence is consistent across multiple activities and is based on large support in both windows. A competing explanation that the differences are only sampling variation in variant frequencies is unlikely given the size and consistency of the relational and positional changes, although the small number of later traces containing A10 means its near-disappearance could partly reflect a rare-variant shift. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, LAG006, LAG007, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]
